claims.text: A minor aluminum addition should be incorporated into the Cr coating during deposition.
Aluminum doping will improve the durability of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
Aluminum doping will reduce Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Aluminum doping will stabilize the oxide scale under combined operational conditions.
Added aluminum will form an Al2O3 interlayer at the Cr/Zr interface.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer will be thin and stable.
The Al2O3 interlayer will act as a diffusion barrier.
The Al2O3 barrier will limit diffusion of Cr into the zirconium substrate at elevated temperatures.
Aluminum doping will preserve the oxidation resistance of the Cr coating in both low- and high-temperature environments.
The Al-doped Cr coating will show less interfacial Cr-Zr transport than an unmodified Cr coating.
The Al-doped Cr coating will maintain better coating integrity than an unmodified Cr coating.
The Al-doped Cr coating will sustain effective oxidation protection relative to an unmodified Cr coating.
The proposed improvement will be particularly evident during high-temperature steam exposure.
Elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of unmodified elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during long-term subcritical-water exposure at approximately 300 degrees Celsius.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during transient steam exposure at approximately 1200 degrees Celsius.
The optimal aluminum concentration for forming the proposed barrier is not known precisely.
The long-term stability of the proposed Al2O3 layer under thermal cycling and neutron irradiation has not been established.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires oxidation protection across both service regimes, but the falsification rule specifies inferior oxidation resistance under both test conditions. Read literally, inferior oxidation resistance in only one regime might not falsify the claimed dual-regime benefit.
